newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end off, dip slightly on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end off, dip slightly on profit-taking.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange closed slightly lower Wednesday with local profit-taking on some leaders offsetting a partial return of foreign cash, brokers said.

"Today, the local investors took profits on certain leaders whose (next) results might not be that good so as to have liquidity to invest in other more attractive shares like the breweries," said Hernando Pastor, of T y J brokerage.
Analysts predicted continued light falls on Thursday.
On Wednesday, the General Index edged down 0.36 percent to 1,551.46 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index fell 0.15 percent to 2,107.21.
Total market volume was an improved but still relatively low 35 million soles ($14 million) on 2,111 trades as 35 stocks fell, 33 were flat and 22 rose.
Volume was boosted by cross trades of 666,365 shares in benchmark Telefonica del Peru and one million shares in food company Fabril Pacifico.

Telefonica fell 0.53 percent to 5.67 soles on a total of 1.558 million shares, which represented a quarter of total market volume, while Fabril dipped 1.32 percent to 3.75 soles on 1.045 million shares.

Breweries were the strongest performers, with Compania Nacional de Cerveza (CNC) up 4.49 percent to 1.63 soles on 2.494 million shares and Cervesur gaining 0.66 percent to 1.53 soles on 16,259 shares.
However, another blue chip, brewery Backus y Johnston, bucked the trend to dip 2.17 percent to 2.70 soles on 373,816 shares.
